sowhat.text: A 3.7% S&P drop and a VIX near 36 will test deal timing, and Fed hike talk keeps financing costly, though high yield spreads were still 352 bp on Thursday. Take-privates like BILL and carve-outs like Mailchimp show sponsors and strategics are still transacting.

pitch: Stocks sold off hard on Friday. The S&P 500 fell 3.7 percent to about 6,910, its seventh straight loss and a correction from the record, and the Nasdaq dropped 5.3 percent as chipmakers like Nvidia fell 14 percent on doubts about AI spending returns. The VIX jumped to about 36. Fed Governor Cook said waiting on rate hikes risks falling behind, but the 10-year still fell 12 basis points to 4.92 percent as investors bought Treasuries. Oil was steady, with WTI near 84 dollars and Brent near 93. On deals, TPG and Corpay agreed to take BILL private for about 6 billion dollars in cash, and Intuit is selling Mailchimp for about 3.7 billion.

quiz.q: Where did the 10-year Treasury yield close on Fri 20 Nov?
Why did the Nasdaq fall 5.3% on 20 Nov?
quiz.a: A chip-led AI rout: Nvidia, Micron and AMD each fell 13% to 14% on doubts that large AI infrastructure spending will earn enough return.

quiz.q: Who is buying BILL Holdings, and for how much?
quiz.a: TPG, with Corpay as a minority investor, for $63.25 a share in cash, about $6.0B of equity value.

chat.a: Friday was a sharp AI-led selloff: the S&P 500 fell 3.7% to 6,910, its seventh straight loss, and the Nasdaq fell 5.3%. The VIX closed at 35.89. Fed hike talk is the backdrop, though the 10-year fell to 4.92%.
chat.tip: Lead with the selloff, then rates.

chat.q: What's your read on oil this week?
chat.a: WTI settled at $83.98 and Brent at $92.57, both up modestly on Friday, a spread of about $9. Oil held up while stocks fell, so energy is not the source of the stress. For energy M&A, steady prices keep buyers and sellers closer on valuation than a sharp move would.
chat.tip: Say oil is not the story this week.

chat.a: TPG and Corpay agreed to take BILL private for about $6.0B in cash. Goldman Sachs and Qatalyst advised BILL, and BofA, Deutsche Bank and RBC advised TPG, with Barclays advising Corpay. Intuit is also selling Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for about $3.68B.
chat.tip: Name the advisers; bankers will ask.

chat.q: What are you watching over the next few weeks?
chat.a: The Dec 8-9 FOMC, after Governor Cook said waiting on hikes risks falling behind the curve, and whether the AI selloff continues after seven straight S&P losses. Both drive financing conditions and deal timing.
chat.tip: Tie each event to financing conditions.

chat.q: Why did Treasury yields fall when the Fed is talking about hikes?
chat.a: The 10-year fell 12 bp to 4.92% as stocks dropped 3.7%, a flight to safety that outweighed hike talk. Short rates stay anchored by the Fed, so the 2-year at 4.63% and 2s10s at +29 bp show the market still sees a positive slope. For M&A, lower long yields help financing but a falling stock market hurts confidence.
chat.tip: Name the two forces, then which one won.

chat.q: If the 10-year rose 50 bp, what happens to a DCF?
chat.a: The 10-year is 4.92% now. A 50 bp rise lifts the risk-free rate and so the WACC, which lowers the present value of cash flows. Long-duration assets with most of their value in the terminal value are hit hardest.
chat.tip: Say the direction, then who is hit hardest.

chat.q: Why would TPG take BILL private after a market drop?
chat.a: A sponsor can buy a public company at a price set before the selloff, with a 31% premium to the 60-day average, and then manage it away from quarterly volatility. High yield spreads at 352 bp on Thursday mean debt is still available, though at a high all-in cost with the Fed possibly hiking. Corpay's minority stake also lowers the sponsor's equity check.
chat.tip: Separate the base rate from the credit spread.
